source_caption:
Paramount Pictures notoriously fought tooth and nail against casting Marlon Brando, dismissing the legendary actor as washed-up, temperamental, and box-office poison. To force the studio’s hand, Francis Ford Coppola shot a secret, makeshift screen test where Brando stuffed his cheeks with tissue paper to look like a bulldog, darkened his hair with shoe polish, and adopted a raspy, whispered cadence. This astonishing physical and psychological transformation didn’t just win him his second Academy Award—it completely revolutionized the cinematic mobster, replacing loud, thuggish aggression with a terrifyingly quiet, patriarchal gravity.
⠀
The Godfather (1972), directed by Francis Ford Coppola, starring Marlon Brando, Al Pacino, James Caan. A masterful, sweeping epic chronicling the violent transfer of power within a New York mafia dynasty, as a reluctant war hero is inexorably drawn into his father’s ruthless criminal empire.

source_details.title: The Godfather
source_details.synopsis: The Godfather is a 1972 American epic gangster film directed by Francis Ford Coppola, who co-wrote the screenplay with Mario Puzo based on Puzo's best-selling 1969 novel. The film features an ensemble cast that includes Marlon Brando, Al Pacino, James Caan, Richard Castellano, Robert Duvall, Sterling Hayden, John Marley, Richard Conte and Diane Keaton. It is the first installment in The Godfather trilogy, which chronicles the Corleone family under patriarch Vito Corleone (Brando) and the transformation of his youngest son, Michael Corleone (Pacino), from reluctant family outsider to ruthless Mafia boss.
